claims.head: Strength vs. Strength
claims.body: The Avalanche are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Lightning are one of the best at keeping shots away. Hot take: the Avalanche break through anyway.
claims.call: The Avalanche’s shot volume score is above 100, the league average, against the Lightning.

claims.call: The Avalanche keep the Lightning’s chances less dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot).

faceoff.text: Anthony Cirelli is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 47% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 27 seconds at a time, against 65 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Brandon Hagel (12 of 19 changes).

notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 6 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Fedor Svechkov takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4. Noah Juulsen is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Burns and Toews.

stakes: The Lightning go in tied for second in the Atlantic with 14 points, the Avalanche tied for fourth in the Central with 11 points.

COL.head: The Avalanche start a half-step ahead
COL.body: Colorado has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage. The Lightning can still swing it if they keep the shots coming.

TBL.head: A slightly uphill night for the Lightning
TBL.body: Colorado has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage. The Lightning’s best way to tip it is piling up shots.
